findings.claim: ImageQueryDropTarget listens on `document` and ignores whether the search modal is open, so while the modal is scoped or browsing (imageEnabled false, so GlobalSearch registers no drop handler) a one-image drop on the modal still reaches the document listener and starts an image query from the page behind it.
findings.impact: On the text-query results page with image search available, opening the modal in scoped or browse mode and dropping one image into it navigates to an image query. The spec says a scoped or browsing modal behaves as when image search is unavailable. This is an edge case for a single user, and nothing is uploaded.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/search/ImageQueryDropTarget.tsx: the document-level dragenter/drop listeners have no check for an open modal. GlobalSearch.tsx sets onDrop to undefined when !imageEnabled, so nothing stops the event before it reaches `document`.
findings.repro: not_reproduced (read only): open /drive/x/search?q=a, open the modal with a scope chip, drag one PNG onto the panel. The document listener classes the drag as one_image and calls onImageQuery.

bucket_proposal.reason: No declared invariant is clearly broken. I7 covers the unavailable state and the modal rules in step 1, and the scoped-modal case is not stated as an invariant.

findings.proposed_fix: Have the modal call stopPropagation on drag events whenever it is open, or have the target skip events whose target is inside the modal.

findings.claim: The document-level `drop` handler calls preventDefault for any drag carrying files, including an upload-class drop, so a drop of a non-image file on the text-query page while image search is available no longer reaches the browser's default (opening the file) as it did before this change.
findings.impact: The drop does nothing instead of the browser opening the file in the tab. This matches the settled reading that an upload-class drop does nothing. The behaviour differs between the available and unavailable states.
findings.evidence: ImageQueryDropTarget.tsx onDrop: `if (!hasFiles(...)) return; event.preventDefault();` runs before the class check.

bucket_proposal.reason: This follows the clarification that an upload-class drop does nothing. It is only a small difference from the pre-change default action.

specification_compliance: I8 on the text-query page: UploadZone is back to its pre-change form, so no upload runs there, which matches the clarification. A one-image drop calls onImageQuery only when the kept class is one_image and the drop holds exactly one image file. The class is set at the first dragenter and is not re-derived on drop.
I7: with onImageQuery undefined the effect registers no listener and the component renders null, so the unavailable state has no wrapper, no handler and no extra DOM.
The earlier r3 findings about the UploadZone wrapper div, the `files.length` term in the overlay condition and the stale refs are gone, because UploadZone.tsx is reverted.
The addon side was not assessed in this round.
potential_unspecified_behavior: Document-level drag listeners on the text-query page also see drags aimed at the open search modal when the modal does not stop them (F1).
A drop of a non-image file on the text-query page is now cancelled with preventDefault while image search is available (F2).
regression_risks: Other document-level drag/drop listeners mounted at the same time, such as the upload store or the file tree, share the same events with this target. Nothing in the diff coordinates them.
The target classifies a drag only at the first dragenter. If a drag enters from outside the window and the depth counter drifts, the overlay can stay up until the next drop or leave.
test_coverage: ImageQueryDropTarget.test.tsx covers one-image search, non-image, several images, unreported type, string item, a class not re-derived on drop, class kept through nested dragenter, and re-classing after leave. All of these dispatch on document.body.

FolderBrowser.imageQuery.test.tsx mocks the target and checks that the prop is passed through. The wrapper-free shape and the mount-once check were deleted with FolderBrowser.imageQuery.upload.test.tsx, so no test covers the unavailable-state DOM or a remount when availability resolves.
No test covers a drop inside the modal while the target is mounted (F1).

trajectory: The design is being simplified. r2 added the `acceptUpload` flag to UploadZone and r3 added an `enabled` flag, both to make the zone pretend to be absent on the search page. This round removes both flags and every image-query branch from UploadZone, restoring the original file. It moves the one-image behaviour into a separate component that renders nothing until a one-image drag. That deletes the earlier states (three zone modes, a drag-class state, a wrapper div) and adds one new component with its own depth counter and class variable. The new component does not repeat the flags of the earlier rounds. The one new risk is a document-level listener that does not know about the modal (F1).
